english.title: Driver of a vehicle in a public place fail give name / address / produce insurance to a constable after an accident
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person whom a constable had reasonable cause to believe to have been the driver of a motor vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), at a time when an accident occurred owing to its presence, in a public place namely, **(..SPECIFY THE PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..), on being so required by a constable or a vehicle examiner, failed to give your name and address and to produce for examination the relevant certificate of insurance under Part VI of the Road Traffic Act 1988
english.legislation: Contrary to section 165(3) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording relates to motor vehicles other than invalid carriages.
(ii) This offence was extended to include 'other public place' by the The Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) Regulations 2000 - S.I. 726/2000 refers.
(iii) Until 1st November 2021, securities or deposits could be used as an alternative to conventional motor insurance. For offences before that date, see H79
english.standardstatementoffacts:
At **(..SPECIFY TIME..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE..) the defendant was suspected of being the driver of **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..) when an accident occurred owing its presence on **(..SPECIFY THE PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..). The defendant failed to give

(A)_[his name and address]_
(B)_[her name and address]_

to a police constable when requested to do so and failed to produce for examination a relevant insurance certificate in respect of the vehicle, when requested to do so, either then or within seven days thereafter.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level three on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
